speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: asked the Minister for Social and Family Development (a) whether persons are eligible for the COVID-19 Support Grant (CSG) even if they have not met the required eligibility of three full months of unemployment; and (b) whether ComCare recipients who may be receiving lower financial support will be disqualified from applying for the CSG.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: CSG was initially designed to support lower to middle income households facing unemployment due to retrenchment or contract termination after 23 January 2020, when the first case of COVID-19 was detected in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Ms Denise Phua asks whether persons are eligible for CSG if they have not met the required eligibility of three full months of unemployment.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The "three or more consecutive months" requirement for NPL and income loss scenarios is to ensure that help is channelled to those who have greater needs.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Individuals who are ineligible for CSG but require further support can apply for ComCare assistance.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Those who are receiving ComCare assistance and who have been further impacted by the pandemic, should be assessed for further assistance under the ComCare scheme and not the CSG.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: ComCare provides monthly cash assistance to low-income households who need help to cover their daily living expenses, including food and other basic living needs.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: ComCare also provides assistance with household bills and medical expenses.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Based on the families’ needs and circumstances, MSF’s Social Service Offices or SSOs, also facilitate their access to other relevant services and support by government agencies and community partners.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: ComCare beneficiaries are invited to approach the SSOs for a review of their current support if their circumstances have changed, for instance, if they have lost their jobs or faced a reduction in income because of the COVID-19 pandemic.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: While reviewing their ComCare support, SSOs can also provide them with interim assistance if they have urgent financial needs.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Those who are newly placed on ComCare will receive at least six months of assistance, providing them with a longer runway to regain stability.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The Government will continue to review how we can better support those who have been adversely impacted due to COVID-19.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Clearly, the Government has covered many grounds to assist citizens and Permanent Residents (PRs) affected by the pandemic.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: The different schemes are administered by different organisations – for example, ComCare applicantions will be administered by MSF, help for the self-employed persons will be by NTUC and I think the drivers who are affected are supported by MOT.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Is there a way by which there is a one-stop clearing house so that a person who is affected will not need to know where to go but they can be directed by the respective personnel who are supporting them, so they know where to go to.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I also want to know if MSF then would exercise flexibility.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Essentially, we need to ensure that agenices who have deep knowledge in the schemes that they administer, to be able to focus on their schemes but also have good awareness about related schemes and programmes that are beneficial to Singaporeans at this time, to be able to make the necessary referrals, link-ups and to also point people in the right direction.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: It is also very important to have good communications to make sure that Singaporeans know where to go to, whom to call, what the eligibility criteria of the different schemes are.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Because of their situation, they tend to be more vulnerable.
